rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause can be circumstantial; that reading sharpens the rebuke because they hope for forgiveness while acting contrary to it.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الحالية أبلغ لأن رجاءهم المغفرة في حال يضادها أوفق بالإنكار عليهم

rows.speaker: الحلبي والسفاقسي
rows.claim: They take the sentence as a new statement, not because a conditional clause cannot be circumstantial, but because that analysis has a Muʿtazilite tendency.
rows.anchor: واختار الحلبي والسفاقسي أن الجملة مستأنفة لا لأن الجملة الشرطية لا تقع حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant is the one in the Torah: the annexation may mean a covenant contained in the Book or a covenant belonging to it; al-kitāb is definite by prior reference.
rows.anchor: أي الميثاق المذكور في التوراة فالإضافة على معنى في ويجوز أن تكون إختصاصية

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may explain the covenant, replace it, state its purpose, or attach to it through an implied preposition; أن may be infinitival or explanatory and لا prohibitive or negative.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان للميثاق وقيل : بدل منه وقيل : إنه مفعول لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heirs are rebuked for asserting that God must forgive them while they persist in sins and repeatedly return to them without repentance.
rows.anchor: أنهم وبخوا على إيجابهم على الله تعالى غفران ذنوبهم التي لا يزالون يعودون إليها ولا يتوبون منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they were reproached for making forgiveness of their recurring, unrepented sins obligatory upon God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهم وبخوا على إيجابهم على الله تعالى غفران ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle س conveys emphatic certainty in their claim of forgiveness, as the authorities state.
rows.anchor: وجاء البت من السين فإنها للتأكيد كما نص عليه المحققون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari accuses Sunnis of sharing the Jews’ view that sin may be forgiven without repentance, and says the Torah conditions forgiveness of grave sins on repentance.
rows.anchor: عرض الزمخشري عامله الله تعالى بعدله في تفسير هذه الآية بأهل السنة وزعم أن مذهبهم هو مذهب اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the comparison: Jews assert forgiveness categorically, while Sunnis do not guarantee it even for the obedient, much less sinners against God or other people.
rows.anchor: فهل ما ادعاه إلا من قبيل ما جاء في المثل

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Zamakhshari derived the Torah claim from this verse, it supports only that Torah distortions included altering prophetic descriptions, the stoning rule, and other laws for bribes and favors.
rows.anchor: إلا على تحريفهم ما في التوراة من نعت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وآية الرجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi notes that al-Zamakhshari himself accepts a comparable divine promise in the Quranic phrase about God forgiving some sins.
rows.anchor: وقد سلم هو نحوا منه قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: شداد بن أوس
rows.claim: Shaddad ibn Aws transmits the Prophet’s saying that the prudent person holds himself accountable and works for the afterlife, while the helpless follows desire and merely hopes in God; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: عن شداد بن أوس أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : الكيس من دان نفسه وعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing includes consuming people’s wealth unjustly, following desire, presuming on God’s mercy, and changing divine rulings to sell them for worldly gain.
rows.anchor: ذموا بأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وإتباع أنفسهم هواها وتمنيهم على الله سبحانه

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had studied the covenant to speak only the Torah’s truth, yet ruled against it, falsely attributed the ruling to God, and sought a small price.
rows.anchor: فلم حكموا بخلافه وقالوا : هو من عند الله وما هو من عند الله ليشتروا به ثمنا قليلا

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jahdari reads أن لا قولوا with a second-person address, using a shift of address.
rows.anchor: الجحدري ( أن لاقولوا ) بالخطاب على الإلتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: درسوا means they read the Book and therefore remember its contents.
rows.anchor: أي قرأوه فهم ذاكرون لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause most naturally coordinates by meaning with the covenant question: the covenant was taken and they studied the Book, despite the difference between declarative and interrogative forms.
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على ( ألم يؤخذ ) من حيث المعنى وإن اختلفا خبرا وإنشاءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses coordinate it directly with لم يؤخذ under the confirming question, with ورثوا while the question is parenthetic, or make the whole intervening question parenthetic.
rows.anchor: وجوز كونه عطفا على ( لم يؤخذ ) والإستفهام التقريري داخل عليهما

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi cites an interpretation of درسوا as abandoning and neglecting the Book when the clause is coordinated with ورثوا; Alusi finds it remote.
rows.anchor: الطبرسي نقل عن بعضهم تفسير درسوا على هذا الوجه من العطف بتركوا وضيعوا وفيه بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal makes the clause circumstantial of the subject of يقولوا, with an implied قد; Alusi considers this strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الجملة في موضع الحال من ضمير يقولوا بإضمار قد

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reads ادارسوا with a doubled د and following alif, from تدارسوا after assimilation of ت into د and insertion of a connecting hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي ( ادارسوا ) بتشديد الدال وألف بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better for those who fear God and His punishment and avoid the heirs’ conduct.
rows.anchor: والدار الآخرة خير للذين يتقون ( الله تعالى ويخافون عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the covenant breakers who take worldly gain as believers intensifies the rebuke; another view addresses believers without a shift of address.
rows.anchor: وهو خطاب لأولئك المأخوذ عليهم الميثاق الآخذين لعرض هذا الأدنى وفي الإلتفات تشديد للتوبيخ

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر وسهل ويعقوب وحفص
rows.claim: Some readers use third-person ياء; Nafi, Ibn Amir, Ibn Dhakwan, Abu Jafar, Sahl, Yaqub, and Hafs use second-person تاء.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمع بالياء على الغيبة وبالتاء وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وابن ذكوان وأبو جعفر

words: أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse plainly rebukes their taking; some locate the reproach in their claim instead, yielding a paired, folded distribution of the two censures.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية ظاهرة في التوبيخ على الأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means holding fast to the Book in religious matters; مسك به and تمسك به are equivalent expressions.
rows.anchor: أي يتمسكون به في أمور دينهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd identify them as believers from the People of the Book, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, who neither distorted nor concealed Moses’ Book nor profited from it.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد : هم الذين آمنوا من أهل الكتاب كعبدالله بن سلام

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata identifies them as Muhammad’s community and takes the Book to mean the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء : هم أمة محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبوبكر وحماد وابن مسعود وأبي
rows.claim: Abu Bakr and Hammad read يمسكون with a light form meaning hold; Ibn Masud reads استمسكوا and Ubay reads مسكوا, agreeing with the following verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبوبكر وحماد ( يمسكون ) بالتخفيف من الإمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known form signals continuous adherence across all times, whereas prayer is performed at prescribed times; prayer is singled out because it is the pillar of religion.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن التمسك أمر مستمر في جميع الأزمنة بخلاف الإقامة فإنها مختصة بالأوقات المخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is singled out from other acts despite being included in adherence to the Book because it surpasses them as the support of religion.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصها بالذكر من بين سائر العبادات مع دخولها بالتمسك بالكتاب لإنافتها عليها لأنها عماد الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause may be genitive, coordinated with الذين يتقون; alternatively it is nominative as a subject whose predicate is إنا لا نضيع.
rows.anchor: محل الموصول إما الجر عطفا على الذين يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the subject analysis, the predicate’s link may be an omitted منهم pronoun per most Basrans, the article per Kufans, or the generic noun المصلحين; alternatively the overt noun replaces an original pronoun and signals that righteousness prevents loss of reward.
rows.anchor: الرابط إما الضمير المحذوف كما هو رأي جمهور البصريين أي أجر المصلحين منهم وإما الألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse supplies a missing predicate, meaning those who hold the Book are rewarded; the promise then parenthetically confirms it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخبر محذوف والتقدير والذين يمسكون بالكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse resumes the preceding command by showing that seeking refuge is the established practice of the Godfearing, while omitting it is the habit of the astray.
rows.anchor: إستئناف مقرر لما قبله من الأمر ببيان أن الإستعاذة سنة مسلوكة للمتقين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains طائف as a touch or whispering suggestion from Satan.
rows.anchor: أي لمة منه كما روي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form belittles the satanic touch; calling it a circuiting visitor suggests it brushes them without affecting them, as though it circles without reaching inside.
rows.anchor: وتنويه للتحقير والمراد وسوسة ما وهو اسم فاعل من طاف بالشيء إذا دار حوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of circling signals that Satan’s whisper touches the Godfearing without penetrating or taking effect.
rows.anchor: وجعل الوسوسة طائفا للإيذان بأنها وإن مست لا تؤثر فيهم فكأنها طافت حولهم ولم تصل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation takes طائف from a dream apparition that visits, making it a passing thought.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون من طاف طيف الخيال إذا ألم في المنام فالمراد به الخاطر

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Several commentators understand طائف as anger.
rows.anchor: وذهب غير واحد إلى أن المراد بالطائف الغضب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, al-Kisai, and Yaqub read طيف, as a verbal noun or a lightened form from a wāw- or yāʾ-root, like هين and لين.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب ( طيف ) على أنه مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan here means the species generally, not Iblis alone, which explains the plural pronoun used later.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشيطان الجنس لا إبليس فقط ولذا جمع ضميره فيما سيأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their remembrance may be of God’s commands and prohibitions, of seeking refuge in God, or of Satan’s enmity and guile.
rows.anchor: أي ما أمر الله تعالى به ونهى عنه أو الإستعاذة به تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through remembrance they recognize errors and paths of right guidance, avoid disobedience, and escape what displeases God.
rows.anchor: مواقع الخطأ ومناهج الرشد فيحترزون عما يخالف أمر الله تعالى وينجون عما لا يرضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative phrase naturally covers everyone characterized by Godfearing, rather than a restricted group.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد من الموصول من اتصف بعنوان الصلة مطلقا

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: An unnamed critical scholar argues that if the earlier address to the Prophet is specific, the Godfearing here should be resolute messengers; if it is general, they are righteous servants.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : إن الخطاب في قوله سبحانه وتعالى : ( وإما ينزغنك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the first conditional’s alleged necessity and says the general reading is the default in every case.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الملازمة في الشرطية الأولى في حيز المنع والعموم هو المتبادر على كل حال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some restrict those touched to non-prophets and the preceding address to Muhammad; they distinguish initial whispering نزغ from a later, established touch مس, as a mark of prophetic favor.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المراد بالمتقين المنسوب إليهم المس غير الأنبياء عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that Satan expends greater effort to whisper to the perfect than to those below, hence نزغ is used earlier and مس here.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال : إن إهتمام الشيطان في الوسوسة للكامل أكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command directs people to the means of attaining the Quran’s great benefits.
rows.anchor: إرشاد إلى طريق الفوز بما أشير إليه من المنافع الجليلة التي ينطوي عليها القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The لام may indicate purpose, mean إلى, or be extra, yielding فاستمعوه.
rows.anchor: واللام جوز أن تكون أجلية وأن تكون بمعنى إلى وأن تكون صلة أي فاستمعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنصات is silence; the related forms mean to be silent, listen silently, or make someone silent, and the verbal noun is النصتة.
rows.anchor: والإنصات السكوت يقال : نصت ينصت وأنصت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjoining silence to listening emphasizes care for the Quran; the purpose is attaining mercy, the highest fruit of its benefits.
rows.anchor: والعطف للإهتمام بأمر القرآن وعلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa uses the verse to require a congregant to listen rather than recite behind the imam in both silent and audible prayers: the command covers Quran recited in prayer and elsewhere, and the non-prayer case has separate permission to listen or not.
rows.anchor: والآية دليل لأبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه في أن المأموم لا يقرأ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that an Ansari man recited behind the Prophet during prayer and this verse was revealed; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : قرأ رجل من الأنصار خلف رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud heard people reciting behind him in prayer, rebuked them after it, and quoted God’s command to listen and be silent.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه صلى بأصحابه فسمع أناسا يقرؤن خلفه فلما انصرف

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says there is no recitation behind the imam.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت قال : لا قراءة خلف الإمام

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s instruction that the imam is followed: when he recites, the congregation should remain silent.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إنما جعل الإمام

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir transmits the Prophetic rule that one praying behind an imam has the imam’s recitation as his own; its transmission and grading are debated in the continuation.
rows.anchor: عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : من كان له إمام فقراءته له قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If sound, the imam report specifies the general command to recite what is easy and the rule that prayer requires recitation; it can also be specified after the agreed exception for one who catches the imam bowing.
rows.anchor: فجاز التخصيص بعده بالمقتدي بالحديث المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative for the person who errs in prayer to recite is read as applying outside following an imam; otherwise the imam’s recitation counts for him and he would have two readings in one prayer.
rows.anchor: فإن قراءة الإمام قراءة له فلو قرأ لكان له قراءتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although many routes raise Jabir’s report to the Prophet, critics who weaken its raised form concede that the sounder transmission is mursal through Musa ibn Abi Aisha and Abdullah ibn Shaddad; Abu Hanifa also transmitted it mursal.
rows.anchor: بأن الصحيح أنه مرسل لأن الحفاظ كالسفيانيين وأبي الأحوص وشعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi answers that the mursal report is authoritative for most scholars and sufficient for his school’s ruling and its dialectical case; even if set aside, Abu Hanifa raised it through a sound chain.
rows.anchor: المرسل حجة عند أكثر أهل العلم

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
rows.claim: In his Muwatta, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan transmits through Abu Hanifa, Musa ibn Abi Aisha, Abdullah ibn Shaddad, and Jabir the Prophet’s ruling that the imam’s recitation counts for the follower.
rows.anchor: وروى محمد بن الحسن في موطئه قال : أنبأنا أبو حنيفة حدثنا

rows.speaker: أحمد بن منيع
rows.claim: Ahmad ibn Maniʿ’s Musnad raises the report through Sufyan and Sharik from Jabir; it also gives Jarir’s version ending at the Prophet without Jabir.
rows.anchor: قال أحمد بن منيع في مسنده : أخبرنا إسحق الأزرق حدثنا سفيان

rows.speaker: عبد بن حميد
rows.claim: Abd ibn Humayd transmits the raised Jabir report through Abu Nuaym, Hasan ibn Salih, and Abu al-Zubayr; Alusi says the first Jabir chain meets the two Ṣaḥīḥs’ standard and the second Muslim’s.
rows.anchor: ورواه عبد بن حميد قال : حدثنا أبو نعيم حدثنا الحسن بن صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the claim that the named hadith masters did not raise the report: Sufyan, Sharik, Jarir, and Abu al-Zubayr did so through sound routes.
rows.anchor: أبو الزبير ورفعوه بالطرق الصحيحة فبطل عدهم فيمن لم يرفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a reliable narrator’s solitary raising would be accepted as an addition by a trustworthy transmitter; here he is not alone, and a transmitter may sometimes connect a report and sometimes transmit it mursal.
rows.anchor: ولو تفرد الثقة وجب قبوله لأن الرفع زيادة وزيادة الثقة مقبولة فكيف ولم ينفرد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والحاكم
rows.claim: A report in Abu Hanifa’s biography, also given by al-Hakim, recounts that a man recited behind the Prophet, a companion forbade him, and the Prophet ruled that the imam’s recitation counts for the follower.
rows.anchor: وذكر فيها قصة وبها أخرجه أبو عبدالله الحاكم

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa’s version locates the incident in the noon or afternoon prayer and says a companion gestured to stop a man reciting behind the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية لأبي حنيفة إن ذلك كان في الظهر أو العصر وهي أن رجلا قرأ خلف رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabir sometimes reports only the legal ruling and sometimes the full incident; because the story supports the companion’s prohibition, especially in a silent prayer, it bars recitation rather than permitting choice.
rows.anchor: إن جابرا روى منه محل الحكم فقط تارة والمجموع تارة ويتضمن رد القراءة خلف الإمام

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reports that after the Prophet’s heavy recitation in dawn prayer, he asked whether they recited behind him; he forbade it except for the Opening of the Book, without which prayer is invalid.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما رواه أبو داود والترمذي عن عبادة بن الصامت قال : كنا خلف رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where the reports conflict, Alusi gives priority to the unrestricted prohibition because it came later and has the stronger chain.
rows.anchor: ويقدم لتقدم المنع على الإطلاق عند التعارض ولقوة السند فإن حديث المنع أصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects partisan criticism of Abu Hanifa’s report method: the Imam required a narrator to recall a report before accepting it even when he recognized his own handwriting, stricter than hadith masters.
rows.anchor: مع تضييقه في الرواية إلى الغاية حتى أنه شرط التذكر لجوازها بعد علم الراوي أن ذلك المروي خطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Jabir reports, though weak, and the reported practice of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn Masud support the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وإن ضعفت وبمذاهب الصحابة أيضا كابن عباس وابن عمر وزيد بن ثابت وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Through Muhammad from Dawud ibn Qays, Umar wishes that a stone were in the mouth of whoever recites behind the imam.
rows.anchor: عن داود بن قيس بن عجلان أن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : ليت في فم

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: A similar statement forbidding recitation behind the imam is also reported from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas.
rows.anchor: وروي مثل ذلك عن سعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali is reported to say that whoever recites behind the imam has erred in the fitra, though Alusi notes a criticism in its transmission.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه إلا أن فيه مقالا أنه قال : من قرأ

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says he met seventy veterans of Badr, all of whom forbade a congregant from reciting behind the imam.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي : أدركت سبعين بدريا كلهم يمنعون المقتدي

rows.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some Hanafis claim the Companions unanimously forbade follower recitation; Alusi says this may mean many leading Companions, since literal or tacit consensus is doubtful.
rows.anchor: وقد ادعى بعض أصحابنا إجماع الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم على ذلك

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير والقاسم بن محمد والزهري ومالك وابن المبارك وأحمد وإسحق
rows.claim: Another group, also reported from Ibn Umar, says the follower recites when the imam is silent but not when he recites aloud, combining the verse’s listening command with the Sunnah’s alleged duty to recite.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن المأموم يقرأ إذا أسر الإمام القراءة ولا يقرأ إذا جهر وهو قول عروة بن الزبير والقاسم بن محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi objects that a silent follower’s not being called a listener does not establish a Sunnah duty to recite; the proof is difficult, and one should follow the stronger evidence.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأنه وإن سلمنا أنه لا يقال له منصت مع علمه بالقراءة وبأنا لا نسلم دلالة السنة على وجوب القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi doubts the report that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan recommended al-Fatiha as a precaution, saying his actual ruling matches Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf in disliking follower recitation under the warning.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا ضعف ما يروى عن محمد بن الحسن رحمه الله تعالى أنه يستحسن قراءة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
rows.claim: In Kitab al-Athar, Muhammad cites Alqama ibn Qays as never reciting behind an imam in either kind of prayer and says this is the rule they follow; his Muwatta gives the same position.
rows.anchor: قال في كتاب الآثار بعد ما أسند إلى علقمة بن قيس : إنه ما قرأ قط

rows.speaker: السرخسي
rows.claim: Al-Sarakhsi says recitation behind the imam invalidates prayer according to several Companions, reportedly including Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas.
rows.anchor: وقال السرخسي تفسد صلاة القاريء خلف الإمام

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The Muzani transmission from al-Shafiʿi has the follower recite in both audible and silent prayers; the Buwaiti transmission has al-Fatiha and a surah in silent prayer, and al-Fatiha alone in audible prayer.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية المزني عن الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه يقرأ في الجهرية والسرية

rows.speaker: الشافعية
rows.claim: The prevalent Shafiʿi view is that a follower who hears the imam in an audible prayer listens without reciting; if he cannot distinguish the words or the prayer is silent, he recites according to the relied-on view.
rows.anchor: والمشهور عند الشافعية أنه لا سورة للمأموم الذي يسمع الإمام في جهرية بل يستمع فإن بعد بأن لم يسمع

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says people used to speak during prayer and this verse was revealed; Alusi distinguishes this occasion from the report about recitation behind the imam.
rows.anchor: فقد روى أبو هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه أنهم كانوا يتكلمون في الصلاة فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some understand القرآن here as the Friday sermon and take listening as obligatory or recommended; Hanafis hold silence during the sermon obligatory, with qualifications.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من فسر القرآن بالخطبة والأمر بالإستماع أما للوجوب أو الندب وعندنا الإنصات في الخطبة فرض

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse applies to prayer and the Friday sermon.
rows.anchor: وأخرج غير واحد عن مجاهد رضي الله تعالى عنه أن الآية في الصلاة والخطبة يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanafi texts indicate a general duty to listen whenever Quran is recited aloud: the Khulasa assigns sin to a reader whose nearby listener cannot attend, including loud night recitation while people sleep.
rows.anchor: قال في الخلاصة : رجل يكتب الفقه وبجنبه رجل يقرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation applies by the wording’s general scope, not just its occasion; إذا expresses universality here, as in most Quranic conditional clauses using it.
rows.anchor: بأن العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب و ( إذا ) هنا للكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of استماع is listening; al-Zajjaj instead figuratively takes it as acceptance and response, as in familiar devotional and royal expressions.
rows.anchor: والمراد من الإستماع في الآية المعنى المتبادر منه وقال الزجاج : المراد منه القبول

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi prefers acceptance and response because it coheres with the preceding and following discourse and gathers the interpretations: believers must accept, act on, and adhere to the Quran.
rows.anchor: ورجح ذلك العلامة الطيبي قال : وهذا أوفق لتأليف النظم الكريم سابقا ولاحقا

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: The context contrasts unbelievers who scorn and reject the Quran with believers instructed to do more than hear: accept it, act by it, and adhere to it for mercy; naming the Quran instead of using a pronoun emphasizes its causal force.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعريضا أن المشركين إنما استهزأوا بالقرآن

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: On al-Tibi’s interpretation, silence in prayer is required a fortiori because prayer is intimate conversation; the command also covers listening when the Prophet recites.
rows.anchor: ويدخل في هذا وجوب الإنصات في الصلاة بطريق الأولى لأنها مقام المناجاة والإستماع من المتكلم

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: This contextual reading makes the addressees believers; al-Tibi says that is explicit in the verse.
rows.anchor: ويعلم منه أن الخطاب في الآية للمؤمنين بل هو نص في ذلك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view addresses unbelievers: if they listen to the Quran at its revelation, they can recognize its inimitability and need no further signs.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن الخطاب فيها للكفار وذلك أن كون القرآن بصائر وهدى ورحمة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Supporters of an unbelieving audience say the hope of mercy suits them, unlike believers already assured of mercy in Quran 45:20.
rows.anchor: في آخر الآية ( لعلكم ترحمون ) بناء على أن ذلك للترجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi answers that the hoped-for mercy may differ from the mercy already stated; even if identical, a generous giver may properly keep hope alive.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن هذه الرحمة المرجوة غير تلك الرحمة ولئن سلم كونها إياها فالأطماع من الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction indicates that the reader may be anyone.
rows.anchor: وفي بناء الفعل للمفعول إشارة إلى أن مدار القراءة من أي قاريء كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some companions recommend honoring Quran recitation outside prayer by wearing one’s best clothes and a turban and facing the qibla; knowledge receives similar honor.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الأصحاب : يستحب لمريد قراءته خارج الصلاة أن يلبس أحسن ثيابه ويتعمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting while reclining is unobjectionable as remembrance, since God praises those who remember standing, sitting, and lying on their sides.
rows.anchor: ولو قرأ مضطجعا فلا بأس إذ هو نوع من الذكر وقد مدح سبحانه ذاكريه قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During recitation one should draw in the legs rather than stretch them, which is poor etiquette; walking or working is acceptable if the heart remains attentive, otherwise it is disliked.
rows.anchor: ويضم رجليه عند القراءة ولا يمدها لأنه سوء أدب ولو قرأ ماشيا أو عند النسج ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not recite with uncovered private parts or in the presence of an uncovered person, even one’s wife; some also dislike reciting in bathhouses and roads.
rows.anchor: ولا يقرأ وهو مكشوف العورة أو كان بحضرته من هو كذلك وإن كانت زوجته وكره بعضهم القراءة في الحمام والطريق

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says the Shafiʿi school does not dislike recitation in bathhouses or roads but does dislike it in a toilet and a mill house while its wheel turns; Alusi says this matches the Hanafi school.
rows.anchor: قال النووي : ومذهبنا لا تكره فيهما وتكره في الحش وبيت الرحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may be part of the commanded speech, with واذكر coordinated to قل, or a fresh divine address to the Prophet that extends to every form of remembrance.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون من القول المأمور به ويحتمل أن تكون إستئنافا من جهته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether direct address or general instruction, inward remembrance is more conducive to sincerity and acceptance.
rows.anchor: وهو عام لكل ذكر فإن الإخفاء أدخل في الإخلاص وأقرب من القبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divine saying promises that God remembers privately the one who remembers Him privately, and remembers in a better assembly one who remembers Him in a gathering; no source or grading is supplied.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار يقول الله تعالى : من ذكرني في نفسه ذكرته في نفسي

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam explains inward remembrance as knowing the meanings of spoken invocations while recalling God’s perfection, power, greatness, and majesty; bare tongue-recitation without inward remembrance is nearly useless.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام : المراد بالذكر في نفسه أن يكون عارفا بمعاني الأذكار

rows.speaker: جمع
rows.claim: Some hold that bare verbal remembrance without attention earns no reward, and that one who says a good word without knowing or considering its meaning is not counted a believer before God.
rows.anchor: ذكر جمع أن الذكر اللساني الساذج لا ثواب فيه أصلا ومن أتى بالكلمة الطيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view addresses the Quran listener, takes remembrance as Quran, and commands the follower to recite quietly after the imam; Alusi considers this remote even if one accepts Abu Hanifa’s position.
rows.anchor: الخطاب لمستمع القرءان والذكر القرءان والمراد أمر المأموم بالقراءة سرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تضرعا وخيفة may be circumstantial, meaning humbly and fearfully, or depend on an omitted noun meaning possessing humility and fear; purpose is not a suitable parse.
rows.anchor: في موضع الحال بتأويل اسم الفاعل أي متضرعا وخائفا أو بتقدير مضاف أي ذا تضرع وخيفة
